## What's new in 0.9.7

Follow-up to 0.9.6, focused on **Orchestrate mode** and the approval prompts that made the agent feel like it was constantly interrupting you.

### Orchestrate mode

- **It delegates now.** Asked to do something, the orchestrator would often just do the whole job itself. Two causes: its instructions explicitly told it to judge whether a task was "small enough to just do yourself", and the rule meant to keep it coordinating only kicked in *after* it had already started a sub-agent — so one that never delegated was never stopped. Investigation stays wide open (it needs to read around before it can write good sub-agent instructions), but making changes now requires delegating first.
- **It stops asking permission to look at things.** Orchestrate was asking you to approve *every* command, including `grep` and `find`. It behaves like Auto now: ordinary work runs, and only genuinely risky commands (`rm`, force-push, `sudo`) pause for you.
- **The sub-agent transcript can be closed** — an ✕ in its header, Escape, or clicking outside the panel.
- **The sub-agent list no longer gets squeezed to nothing.** A long sub-agent reply used to crowd the list out, so with several sub-agents you'd see one row and no way back. The split between the list and the transcript is fixed now regardless of how much a sub-agent wrote.

### Agent mode

- **Read-only commands stop prompting.** Any command capturing its output with `2>&1` — extremely common — was misread as writing to a file, so `./gradlew build 2>&1 | tail`, `npm test 2>&1`, even `git status 2>&1` all asked for approval. Fixed, along with the mirror-image case where `echo x > out.txt 2>/dev/null` was wrongly treated as harmless. `npx tsc --noEmit` also runs unasked now; bare `npx tsc` still asks, because it writes files.

### Elsewhere

- **Installed-app tools show the "running" spinner** while they work, like every other tool — a slow app tool no longer looks like the agent has stalled.

### Under the hood

The Code engine — which also powers Create, Auto and Orchestrate — was split into focused modules: the tool dispatch into per-tool-family handlers, the chat pane into components, and the six duplicated per-section settings objects into one factory. Test coverage doubled (11 → 22 suites), including the first real tests for the tool-dispatch layer and for the command-approval rules, both of which had none. Two of the bugs above were found by writing those tests rather than by hitting them.

No action needed — open installs will offer the update automatically.
